claim: Tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM) protect from repeat infections within organs and barrier sites.
source: Tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM) protect from repeat infections within organs and barrier sites.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that is part of established scientific knowledge about TRM function.

claim: CD69+CD4+ TRM in skin reside for approximately 24 days.
source: We show that CD69+CD4+ TRM in skin reside for ∼24 days and self-renew more slowly, such that clones halve in size approximately every 5 weeks, and approximately 2% of cells are replaced daily from precursors.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from fate mapping experiments and mathematical modeling presented in the manuscript.

claim: CD69+CD4+ TRM in skin self-renew such that clones halve in size approximately every 5 weeks.
source: We show that CD69+CD4+ TRM in skin reside for ∼24 days and self-renew more slowly, such that clones halve in size approximately every 5 weeks, and approximately 2% of cells are replaced daily from precursors.
evidence: This is derived from mathematical modeling of the experimental fate mapping data.

claim: Approximately 2% of CD69+CD4+ TRM cells in skin are replaced daily from precursors.
source: We show that CD69+CD4+ TRM in skin reside for ∼24 days and self-renew more slowly, such that clones halve in size approximately every 5 weeks, and approximately 2% of cells are replaced daily from precursors.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the mathematical modeling of experimental data.

claim: CD69+CD4+ TRM in LP have shorter residencies of approximately 14 days.
source: CD69+CD4+ TRM in LP have shorter residencies (∼14 days) and are maintained largely by immigration (4–6% per day).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experimental data and modeling analysis.

claim: CD69+CD4+ TRM in LP are maintained largely by immigration at 4-6% per day.
source: CD69+CD4+ TRM in LP have shorter residencies (∼14 days) and are maintained largely by immigration (4–6% per day).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the mathematical modeling of experimental data.

claim: The continuous replacement of CD69+CD4+ TRM at both sites derives from circulating effector-memory CD4+ T cells.
source: We also find evidence that the continuous replacement of CD69+CD4+ TRM at both sites derives from circulating effector-memory CD4+ T cells, in skin possibly via a local CD9− intermediate.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the model comparison analysis showing which precursor populations best explain the data.

claim: In skin, CD69+CD4+ TRM replacement possibly occurs via a local CD69− intermediate.
source: We also find evidence that the continuous replacement of CD69+CD4+ TRM at both sites derives from circulating effector-memory CD4+ T cells, in skin possibly via a local CD9− intermediate.
evidence: This is inferred from model comparison showing CD69− cells as the favored precursor in skin.

claim: Conventional CD4+ and CD8+ TRM in mice and humans are not intrinsically long-lived.
source: Conventional CD4+ and CD8+ TRM in mice and humans are not intrinsically long-lived, but appear to self-renew slowly as assessed by readouts of cell division such Ki67 expression or BrdU incorporation, at levels that vary across tissues (Gebhardt et al., 2009; Watanabe et al., 2015; Park et al., 2018; Strobl et al., 2020; Divito et al., 2020; Christo et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: TRM appear to self-renew slowly as assessed by readouts of cell division such as Ki67 expression or BrdU incorporation, at levels that vary across tissues.
source: Conventional CD4+ and CD8+ TRM in mice and humans are not intrinsically long-lived, but appear to self-renew slowly as assessed by readouts of cell division such Ki67 expression or BrdU incorporation, at levels that vary across tissues (Gebhardt et al., 2009; Watanabe et al., 2015; Park et al., 2018; Strobl et al., 2020; Divito et al., 2020; Christo et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: In the lung there is evidence both for and against ongoing recruitment of new TRM following respiratory virus infections.
source: For example, in the lung there is evidence both for (Zammit et al., 2006; Ely et al., 2006; Slütter et al., 2017; Van Braeckel-Budimir et al., 2018; Takamura and Kohlmeier, 2019) and against (Takamura et al., 2016; Bullock et al., 2024, van Dorp et al., 2025) ongoing recruitment of new TRM following respiratory virus infections.
evidence: This statement summarizes conflicting findings from multiple cited studies.

claim: Within skin, TRM may be renewed or supplemented slowly from precursors in the setting of graft-versus-host disease.
source: Within skin, TRM may be renewed or supplemented slowly from precursors in the setting of graft-versus-host disease (Divito et al., 2020), and from circulating central memory TCM or effector memory TEM following infection or sensitisation (Gaide et al., 2015; Matos et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Skin TRM may be renewed from circulating central memory TCM or effector memory TEM following infection or sensitisation.
source: Within skin, TRM may be renewed or supplemented slowly from precursors in the setting of graft-versus-host disease (Divito et al., 2020), and from circulating central memory TCM or effector memory TEM following infection or sensitisation (Gaide et al., 2015; Matos et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In the small intestine, resident CD4+ and CD8+ TRM appear to persist for months to years with slow self-renewal without appreciable influx.
source: In the small intestine, however, resident CD4+ and CD8+ TRM appear to persist for months to years with slow self-renewal without appreciable influx (Bartolomé-Casado et al., 2019; Bartolomé-Casado et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The balance of loss and self-renewal defines the persistence of clonal populations and hence the duration of protective immunity.
source: The balance of loss and self-renewal defines the persistence of clonal populations and hence the duration of protective immunity.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the relationship between cellular dynamics and immunity.

claim: Self-renewal can at best preserve clonal diversity within a tissue site.
source: Further, while self-renewal can at best preserve clonal diversity within a tissue site, any supplementation or replacement by immigrant TRM will perturb the local TCR repertoire.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the effects of different cellular processes on diversity.

claim: Any supplementation or replacement by immigrant TRM will perturb the local TCR repertoire.
source: Further, while self-renewal can at best preserve clonal diversity within a tissue site, any supplementation or replacement by immigrant TRM will perturb the local TCR repertoire.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the effects of immigration on TCR diversity.

claim: Any significant influx into TRM niches in the absence of overt infection may be a competitive force, potentially reducing the persistence of TRM previously established in response to infection or challenge.
source: In particular, any significant influx into TRM niches in the absence of overt infection may be a competitive force, potentially reducing the persistence of TRM previously established in response to infection or challenge.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential competitive effects.

claim: Ki67 is a nuclear protein expressed during cell division and for 3-4 days afterwards.
source: In the Ki67mCherry-CreERT Rosa26RcagYFP system, henceforth Ki67-DIVN, fluorescent reporters are linked to the expression of Ki67, a nuclear protein expressed during cell division and for 3–4 days afterwards (Gossel et al., 2017; Miller et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies characterizing Ki67 expression kinetics.

claim: The skin- and LP-localised T cell subsets considered were at, or close to, homeostatic equilibrium during the chase period.
source: We therefore assumed that the skin- and LP-localised T cell subsets we considered were at, or close to, homeostatic equilibrium during the chase period.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of significant changes in cell numbers over time.

claim: mTom expression within the skin and LP subsets declined slowly, roughly seven- to eight-fold over the course of a year.
source: A key observation was that mTom expression within the skin and LP subsets then declined slowly (roughly seven- to eight-fold over the course of a year, Figure 2C), indicating immediately that these populations were being continuously replaced from precursors.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The decline in mTom expression indicates that skin and LP T cell populations were being continuously replaced from precursors.
source: A key observation was that mTom expression within the skin and LP subsets then declined slowly (roughly seven- to eight-fold over the course of a year, Figure 2C), indicating immediately that these populations were being continuously replaced from precursors.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed decline in mTom expression.

claim: Early in the chase period YFP+ TRM expressed Ki67 at higher levels than YFP− cells.
source: Early in the chase period YFP+ TRM expressed Ki67 at higher levels than YFP− cells, as expected, but Ki67 expression in the two populations converged at later times.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Ki67 expression in YFP+ and YFP− TRM populations converged at later times.
source: Early in the chase period YFP+ TRM expressed Ki67 at higher levels than YFP− cells, as expected, but Ki67 expression in the two populations converged at later times.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The mean residence times of both EM and TRM within skin were approximately 3 weeks.
source: The mean residence times of both EM and TRM within skin and LP were ∼3 weeks and 2 weeks, respectively.
evidence: This is a result from the mathematical modeling of the experimental data.

claim: The mean residence times of both EM and TRM within LP were approximately 2 weeks.
source: The mean residence times of both EM and TRM within skin and LP were ∼3 weeks and 2 weeks, respectively.
evidence: This is a result from the mathematical modeling of the experimental data.

claim: In skin, around 2% of both EM and TRM populations were replaced daily by influx.
source: In skin, around 2% of both populations were replaced daily by influx, comparable to the rates of constitutive replacement of circulating memory CD4+ T cell subsets (Gossel et al., 2017; Hogan et al., 2019; Bullock et al., 2024), and EM and TRM self-renewed every 6 and 7 weeks, respectively.
evidence: This is a result from the mathematical modeling of the experimental data.

claim: The rate of replacement of skin TRM is comparable to the rates of constitutive replacement of circulating memory CD4+ T cell subsets.
source: In skin, around 2% of both populations were replaced daily by influx, comparable to the rates of constitutive replacement of circulating memory CD4+ T cell subsets (Gossel et al., 2017; Hogan et al., 2019; Bullock et al., 2024), and EM and TRM self-renewed every 6 and 7 weeks, respectively.
evidence: This is a comparison to previous studies cited in the text.

claim: Skin EM self-renewed every 6 weeks.
source: In skin, around 2% of both populations were replaced daily by influx, comparable to the rates of constitutive replacement of circulating memory CD4+ T cell subsets (Gossel et al., 2017; Hogan et al., 2019; Bullock et al., 2024), and EM and TRM self-renewed every 6 and 7 weeks, respectively.
evidence: This is a result from the mathematical modeling of the experimental data.

claim: Skin TRM self-renewed every 7 weeks.
source: In skin, around 2% of both populations were replaced daily by influx, comparable to the rates of constitutive replacement of circulating memory CD4+ T cell subsets (Gossel et al., 2017; Hogan et al., 2019; Bullock et al., 2024), and EM and TRM self-renewed every 6 and 7 weeks, respectively.
evidence: This is a result from the mathematical modeling of the experimental data.

claim: Within LP, EM and TRM divided less often (every 7-9 weeks) compared to skin.
source: In contrast, within LP these subsets divided less often (every 7–9 weeks) and relied on higher levels of recruitment (4–6% per day) for their maintenance.
evidence: This is a result from the mathematical modeling of the experimental data.

claim: LP EM and TRM relied on higher levels of recruitment (4-6% per day) for their maintenance.
source: In contrast, within LP these subsets divided less often (every 7–9 weeks) and relied on higher levels of recruitment (4–6% per day) for their maintenance.
evidence: This is a result from the mathematical modeling of the experimental data.

claim: The substantial rates of self-renewal in skin led to clonal half lives of just over a month.
source: The substantial rates of self-renewal in skin led to clonal half lives of just over a month.
evidence: This is derived from the mathematical modeling results.

claim: The lower levels of self-renewal and higher levels of replacement in LP resulted in shorter clonal half lives of approximately 2 weeks.
source: The lower levels of self-renewal and higher levels of replacement in LP resulted in shorter clonal half lives of approximately 2 weeks.
evidence: This is derived from the mathematical modeling results.

claim: The duration of Ki67 expression was approximately 3 days.
source: This quantity in turn was informative for estimating rates of self-renewal. Further, the observed convergence of Ki67 expresssion within these two subsets is consistent with the assumption of homogeneity in the rates of division and loss within skin and LP.
evidence: This is inferred from the modeling of Ki67 convergence kinetics and is consistent with previous estimates mentioned in the text.

claim: The observed convergence of Ki67 expression within YFP+ and YFP− subsets is consistent with the assumption of homogeneity in the rates of division and loss within skin and LP.
source: Further, the observed convergence of Ki67 expresssion within these two subsets is consistent with the assumption of homogeneity in the rates of division and loss within skin and LP.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed data pattern.

claim: Lymph-node-derived EM was strongly favoured as the closest precursor to CD4+ EM within both skin and LP.
source: We found that the data were quite strongly informative regarding the immediate ancestors of tissue subsets. From the candidate set of models, the weighting strongly favoured lymph-node-derived EM as the closest precursor to CD4+ EM within both skin and LP.
evidence: This is a result from the model comparison analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Within skin, local CD69− cells were the favoured precursor to CD69+ TRM.
source: However, within skin, local CD69− cells were the favoured precursor to CD69+ TRM.
evidence: This is a result from the model comparison analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: There was substantial evidence (66% of model support) for a division-linked transition from CD69− to CD69+ cells in skin.
source: The evidence was generally more equivocal regarding the mode in which cells are recruited into skin and LP, although for skin we saw substantial evidence (66% of model support) for a division-linked transition from CD69− to CD69+ cells.
evidence: This is a result from the model comparison analysis.

claim: Using Ki67 expression frequency and daily replacement rate, residence times in skin were estimated to be in the range 22-28 days.
source: In skin, both EM and TRM are replaced at the rate of 2% per day and have Ki67 expression frequencies of around 0.15 (Figure 2C). The approximation then yields residence times in the range 22–28 days, depending on whether immigrant TRM are Ki67low or Ki67high, respectively.
evidence: This is a validation calculation using an independent method based on Ki67 expression.

claim: Using Ki67 expression frequency and daily replacement rate, residence times in LP were estimated to be 14-25 days.
source: In LP, with 5.5% daily replacement and Ki67 frequencies of around 0.07, we estimate residence times of 14–25 days.
evidence: This is a validation calculation using an independent method based on Ki67 expression.

claim: The residence time estimates from Ki67-based approximation are in good agreement with those from the model fitting.
source: Both estimates are in good agreement with those from the model fitting.
evidence: This is a comparison between two different analytical approaches.

claim: CD4+ TRM are not intrinsically long-lived, but instead are sustained by both self-renewal and supplementation from circulating precursors.
source: Our analysis indicates that CD4+ TRM are not intrinsically long-lived, but instead are sustained by both self-renewal and supplementation from circulating precursors.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the combined experimental and modeling analysis.

claim: There are distinct contributions of recruitment and self-renewal of both subsets within skin and LP.
source: We saw quite distinct contributions of recruitment and self-renewal of both subsets within skin and LP.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling results comparing the two tissues.

claim: The large antigenic burden within the small intestine may drive the higher levels of TRM recruitment and clonal erosion within the LP.
source: The basis of this difference is unclear, but we speculate that the large antigenic burden within the small intestine drives the higher levels of TRM recruitment and clonal erosion within the LP.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed differences between tissues.

claim: YFP levels among naive T cells were probably sustained to an extent by low-level residual labelling of thymic progenitors.
source: YFP levels among naive T cells were also probably sustained to an extent by low-level residual labelling of thymic progenitors (Lukas et al., 2023).
evidence: This is an inference supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: All CD4+ T cell subsets within skin and LP tissues were at steady state.
source: Our analysis was rooted in the observation that all CD4+ T cell subsets within these tissues were at steady state.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental observations of stable cell numbers.

claim: Dynamic equilibrium dictates that immigration of new cells must be accompanied by loss of existing ones.
source: This dynamic equilibrium dictates that immigration of new cells must be accompanied by loss of existing ones.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the concept of steady state.

claim: The dynamic populations studied are likely specific for self or commensal antigens that are continuously expressed in SPF mice.
source: In the SPF mice studied here, these dynamic populations are likely specific for self or commensal antigens that are continuously expressed.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental context and known biology of SPF mice.

claim: Residence and interdivision times may be distinct for TRM that are not replenished long-term from precursors, such as those generated in acute infections.
source: It is possible that residence and interdivision times are distinct for TRM that might not be replenished long-term from precursors, such as those generated in acute infections.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential differences in other contexts.

claim: The simple model can explain the stable maintenance of TRM numbers in healthy skin and LP without needing to invoke the concept of a homeostatic niche.
source: Further, our simple model can explain the stable maintenance of TRM numbers in healthy skin and LP without needing to invoke the concept of a homeostatic niche, such as a competitive limit to cell densities.
evidence: This is an inference from the modeling results.

claim: Any increase or decrease in the rate of influx into a tissue will simply lead to a new equilibrium at higher or lower cell densities, respectively.
source: In this model, any increase or decrease in the rate of influx into a tissue will simply lead to a new equilibrium at higher or lower cell densities, respectively.
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model.

claim: Repeated vaccinia virus challenges can drive progressive increases in the number of virus-specific CD8+ TRM in skin that are detectable for months.
source: Indeed repeated vaccinia virus challenges can drive progressive increases in the number of virus-specific CD8+ TRM in skin that are detectable for months (Jiang et al., 2012), and heterologous challenges appear not to erode pre-existing LCMV-specific CD8+ TRM (Wijeyesinghe et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Heterologous challenges appear not to erode pre-existing LCMV-specific CD8+ TRM.
source: Indeed repeated vaccinia virus challenges can drive progressive increases in the number of virus-specific CD8+ TRM in skin that are detectable for months (Jiang et al., 2012), and heterologous challenges appear not to erode pre-existing LCMV-specific CD8+ TRM (Wijeyesinghe et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Whether the same flexibility manifests among CD4+ TRM following repeated challenges is unclear.
source: However, whether the same flexibility manifests among CD4+ TRM following repeated challenges is unclear.
evidence: This acknowledges a gap in current knowledge.

claim: CD69+CD4+ TRM in skin derive at least in part from a local CD69− precursor.
source: We found evidence that CD69+CD4+ TRM in skin derive at least in part from a local CD69− precursor.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the model comparison analysis.

claim: The highly dynamic nature of CD4+ TRM is sustained throughout life by both self-renewal and continued influx from precursors.
source: Nevertheless, our study clearly exposes the highly dynamic nature of CD4+ TRM, sustained throughout life by both self-renewal and continued influx from precursors.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the combined experimental and modeling analysis.

claim: Tissue-specific influx, particularly if there are competitive limits to TRM occupancy, may contribute to the differential longevity of immunity at different barrier sites.
source: This tissue-specific influx, particularly if there are competitive limits to TRM occupancy, may contribute to the differential longevity of immunity at different barrier sites.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential implications of the findings.

claim: Ki67-DIVN mice express both a Ki67-mCherry fusion protein and inducible CreERT from the Mki67 locus, together with a Rosa26RcagYFP Cre reporter construct.
source: Specifically, these mice express both a Ki67-mCherry fusion protein and inducible CreERT from the Mki67 locus, together with a Rosa26RcagYFP Cre reporter construct.
evidence: This is a description of the genetic construct used in the study.

claim: Treatment of Ki67-DIVN mice with tamoxifen induces YFP in cells expressing high levels of Ki67, and YFP is then stably expressed by these cells and their offspring.
source: Treatment of mice with tamoxifen therefore induces YFP in cells expressing high levels of Ki67, and YFP is then stably expressed by these cells and their offspring.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of the fate reporter system.

claim: Expression of Ki67-fused mCherry gives a constitutive live readout of Ki67 expression, independent of tamoxifen treatment and YFP expression.
source: Expression of Ki67-fused mCherry gives a constitutive live readout of Ki67 expression, independent of tamoxifen treatment and YFP expression.
evidence: This describes a feature of the reporter system.

claim: In CD4CreERT Rosa26RmTom mice, cells expressing CD4 during tamoxifen treatment permanently and heritably express the fluorescent reporter mTomato.
source: In the second fate reporter, CD4CreERT Rosa26RmTom mice (Cd4-FR), the Cre reporter is constructed such that cells expressing CD4 during tamoxifen treatment permanently and heritably express the fluorescent reporter mTomato (mTom).
evidence: This describes the mechanism of the second fate reporter system.

claim: Less than 3% of cells recovered from tissue samples were positive for in vivo Thy1.2 labeling, supporting the assumption of very low rates of false-positive and false-negative events.
source: This protocol typically achieves >99% staining of circulating cells (Anderson et al., 2014), and less than 3% of cells recovered from our tissue samples were label positive (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), supporting the assumption of very low rates of false-positive and false-negative events.
evidence: This is a validation of the tissue localization method using experimental data and a citation.

claim: CD4+ TRM typically outnumber their CD8+ counterparts.
source: Far less is known regarding CD4+ TRM, which typically outnumber their CD8+ counterparts (Szabo et al., 2019), and there have been very few attempts to dissect the kinetics of either subset (Bullock et al., 2024, van Dorp et al., 2025).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: There have been very few attempts to dissect the kinetics of CD4+ or CD8+ TRM subsets.
source: Far less is known regarding CD4+ TRM, which typically outnumber their CD8+ counterparts (Szabo et al., 2019), and there have been very few attempts to dissect the kinetics of either subset (Bullock et al., 2024, van Dorp et al., 2025).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field supported by citations.

claim: Division-linked labelling alone may not distinguish in situ cell division and the supplementation of a population from labelled precursors.
source: In general, measuring these basic parameters in isolation is challenging, partly due to their sensitivity to assumptions made in the models (De Boer and Perelson, 2013), but also because division-linked labelling alone may not distinguish in situ cell division and the supplementation of a population from labelled precursors.
evidence: This is a statement about methodological challenges supported by a citation.

claim: These issues can be addressed by modelling different readouts of cell fate simultaneously.
source: These issues can be addressed by modelling different readouts of cell fate simultaneously (Bains et al., 2009; den Braber et al., 2012; Costa Del Amo et al., 2018; De Boer and Yates, 2023; Bullock et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous methodological studies.

claim: Modelling has established evidence for continuous replenishment of circulating memory CD4+ T cells from precursors throughout life in specific-pathogen-free mice.
source: Modelling has also established evidence for continuous replenishment of circulating memory CD4+ T cells from precursors throughout life in specific-pathogen-free mice, driven by a combination of environmental, commensal, and self antigens (Gossel et al., 2017; Hogan et al., 2019; Bullock et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous modeling studies.

claim: Continuous replenishment of circulating memory CD4+ T cells is driven by a combination of environmental, commensal, and self antigens.
source: Modelling has also established evidence for continuous replenishment of circulating memory CD4+ T cells from precursors throughout life in specific-pathogen-free mice, driven by a combination of environmental, commensal, and self antigens (Gossel et al., 2017; Hogan et al., 2019; Bullock et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.
